result:
Solution 1 is the best match for the intended answer, though I could not prove its "if and only if" claim for every group.

Since r ≥ 1, write V* = (V*)^G ⊕ W with W^G = 0. Then R ≅ k[x₁,…,x_r] ⊗ k[W]^G, so the Hilbert series is (1−t)^(−r) times the Hilbert series of k[W]^G. The second factor has Krull dimension d−r and no invariant linear forms.

- The pole at t = 1 has order d, so it contributes constant coefficients to every a_i.
- A pole at a root of unity ζ ≠ 1 can only come from the k[W]^G part. Its order is at most d−r, because the factor (1−t)^(−r) is analytic at ζ. Such a pole contributes terms n^j ζ^(−n) with j ≤ d−r−1, so these are the only possible periodic, non-constant terms.
- Hence a_i is constant for every i ≥ d−r.

The converse can fail for particular groups. Take Z/3 acting on W = k² with eigenvalues ω, ω², and add one trivial coordinate, so d = 3 and r = 1. The poles at ω and ω² are simple, so a₁ is constant even though 1 < d−r = 2.

The problem asks for a single answer in terms of d and r, so I take the intended statement to be that exactly a_{d−r}, …, a_{d−1} are constant. This is the generic case; for example, G = {±1} acting on W = k² gives a double pole at t = −1. The sum is

∑_{i=d−r}^{d−1} i = r(2d − r − 1)/2.

Check at r = d (trivial action): every coefficient is constant, and the formula gives d(d−1)/2, which is correct.

Solution 2 is wrong because it claims all a_i with i ≥ 1 are constant regardless of r, which fails, for example, for Z/2 acting on k³ with r = 1. Solution 3 is wrong because it keeps only i = d−1 and ignores the other constant coefficients for r ≥ 2.

CHOICE: 1
